items.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020
items.q: then Snooky Young stood next to me on Louie Bellson’s band for a long time

ctx.x: Well for me, I was on Gerald’s band playing the lead chair for a while, and then Snooky Young stood next to me on Louie Bellson’s band for a long time and he was also, we were in Bill Berry’s band together and also in the Juggernaut, Nat Pierce/Frank Capp band together. I love Snooky. My three favorite lead trumpet players in the world are Snooky, Al Porcino and Conrad Gozzo. Anybody that’s going to learn to play lead trumpet better study those three guys because everybody else comes from those three.

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Bobby Shew would not play any jazz as long as Blue was in the band.

ctx.x: Bobby Shew would not play any jazz as long as Blue was in the band. He loved Blue Mitchell. Then when Blue Mitchell passed away, then Bobby started playing jazz too. But he loved Blue so much. He said, “As long as Blue’s here, he’s the boss.” Blue Mitchell was great, a great performer, a great guy.
What else can you say about Blue, since he’s overshadowed in the history of jazz, and here you had a really . . .?
